check: The HD 181327 debris ring rendered in the application from Earth's direction, against the paper's reflectance-colour panel

reference.figure: Gáspár et al. (2026), arXiv:2608.27437v1, Figure 1, HD 181327 panel
reference.scale: 32 figure pixels per arcsecond, from the panel's 1-arcsecond bar
reference.note: The figure is read, not retained here.

method: Headless Chromium, 1440 x 900 px at device scale 1, the local dev server, /hd-181327/?dataset=debris-ring: the star's default view, which looks from Earth with celestial north up, zoomed out past 700 au, the shell hidden. The render is registered to the panel with its scale fitted and no rotation or mirror allowed; brightness is compared as median luminance in rings from 1.25 to 4.4 arcsec, each over its own ring peak. The long axis and axis ratio come from an ellipse fitted to the ridge, the radius of peak brightness in 72 azimuths, on each image.

topAlpha.note: the one renderer setting a source cannot give; 0.5 matches the published profile best

known: The render is darker than the printed figure overall (0.48 of its ring brightness): in the renderer's emission model brightness and see-through are one number, and a printed figure is an opaque picture.
